why:
the C logging surface, reachable from the umbrella header since issue 0795 was fixed (`rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp` always included its C++ twin). ROS 2's counterpart is rcutils logging. CORRECTION (2026-09-13): this row said we decline it as a whole "because it carries per-logger level maps, an installable output handler and a formatted-message buffer per thread" and that "ours emits through the platform sink the board installed". Two of those three shipped in phase-417 W4.d — a bounded per-logger level table (`rclc_log_get_logger` + `rclc_logger_set_level`) and an installable sink (`rclc_log_add_sink`, which APPENDS to the board's rather than replacing it). The per-thread formatted-message buffer is still declined: `NROS_LOG_FMT_BUFFER_SIZE` is a 256-byte stack buffer at the call site, because a per-thread buffer needs an allocator or a thread-count bound and neither exists here. What the rest of this row argues — that there is no logger HANDLE type in rcutils to correlate against — is unaffected. This is the entry point a C author must find FIRST: reaching for `printf` instead is fatal on Zephyr native_sim (issue 0589), which is why the umbrella omitting it was a hazard and not just a discoverability nit.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. W2 F14, and the finding's wording NARROWED: rcutils has no logger HANDLE type at all — its API is `rcutils_log(location, severity, const char *name, format, ...)` — so the pointer a porting user most plausibly hands us is the logger NAME (`const char *`), and rclcpp's is an `rclcpp::Logger` object. Say "any pointer, including a logger name", not "an rcutils logger type".

THE FINDING: `typedef const void *rclc_logger_t` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/rclc/log.h`) is the parameter type of ten functions (`rclc_log_emit`, `rclc_log_emit_fmt`, the two `_at` forms, `rclc_log_default_logger`, `rclc_log_get_logger`, `rclc_logger_get_name`, `rclc_logger_set_level`, `rclc_logger_get_level`, `rclc_logger_is_enabled`). In C every object pointer converts to `const void *` implicitly, with no diagnostic at any warning level, and the Rust side then does `&*(logger as *const nros_log::Logger)` unconditionally (`packages/api/nros-c/src/log.rs`), checking only for NULL.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: SILENTLY WRONG, THEN UB — the wrong pointer is dereferenced as a `Logger` and its name and level are read out of whatever bytes are there. NULL is the only value handled, and it is also what `rclc_node_get_logger` returns for an uninitialised node, so the two failure modes are indistinguishable at the call site.

RFC-0089 says a refusal fires at the earliest point the defect is KNOWABLE, and for a pointer type that point is the TYPE: an opaque `struct nros_logger_s *` would make the mistake a compile error and costs nothing at runtime. The `extension` verdict above is unchanged — rcutils logging is declined as a whole — but the opaque-handle shape is the disposition this item should carry once the family is decided. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

NO DISPOSITION IS WRITTEN on this row. The four dispositions are what clause 1 does to a CANDIDATE FROM CLAUSE 2 (RFC-0089), and the row's `extension` verdict rests on rcutils logging being declined as a whole, so the handle type has no upstream counterpart to adopt or refuse. The opaque-struct shape argued above is the fix for the CONVERSION hazard, not a disposition, and the family's own disposition belongs to whatever settles the rcutils decline.
